# -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Server & Spring Boot
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
server:
  # Uncomment to serve FHIR under a non-default context path (e.g., /example/path/fhir)
  # servlet:
  #   context-path: /example/path
  port: 8085
  tomcat:
    # allow | as a separator in URLs
    relaxed-query-chars: "|"

management:
  # Actuator endpoints: only /actuator/health exposed by default
  endpoints:
    access:
      default: none
    web:
      exposure:
        include: "health"  # or "info,health,prometheus,metrics" or "*" for all
  endpoint:
    info:
      access: read_only
    metrics:
      access: read_only
    health:
      access: read_only
      probes:
        enabled: true
      group:
        liveness:
          include: [ "livenessState" ]
        readiness:
          include: [ "readinessState" ]
    prometheus:
      access: read_only
  prometheus:
    metrics:
      export:
        enabled: true

spring:
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # A. Spring AI — Model Context Protocol (MCP)
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ai:
    # Run e.g. `npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector` and connect to http://localhost:8080/mcp/messages using Streamable HTTP

    # Add the following to the MCP server settings file in e.g. cursor or claude (Desktop applications) for local debugging:
    #    cursor:
    #    {
    #      "mcpServers": {
    #        "hapi": {
    #          "url": "http://localhost:8080/mcp/messages"
    #        }
    #      }
    #    }
    #    or claude:
    #    {
    #      "mcpServers": {
    #        "hapi": {
    #          "command": "npx",
    #          "args": [
    #            "mcp-remote@latest",
    #            "http://localhost:8080/mcp/messages"
    #          ]
    #        }
    #      }
    #    }

    mcp:
      server:
        name: FHIR MCP Server
        version: 1.0.0
        instructions: "This server provides access to a FHIR RESTful API. You can use it to query FHIR resources, perform operations, and retrieve data in a structured format."
        enabled: true
        streamable-http:
          mcp-endpoint: /mcp/messages


  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # B. Core Spring
  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  main:
    allow-bean-definition-overriding: false
    allow-circular-references: true

  autoconfigure:
    # This exclude is only needed for setups not using Elasticsearch where the elasticsearch sniff is not needed.
    exclude: org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.elasticsearch.ElasticsearchRestClientAutoConfiguration

  flyway:
    enabled: false
    baseline-on-migrate: true
    fail-on-missing-locations: false

  datasource:
    # url: "jdbc:h2:file:./target/database/h2"
    url: jdbc:h2:mem:test_mem
    username: sa
    password: null
    driver-class-name: org.h2.Driver
    # max-active: 15     # (ignored with HikariCP; use hikari.maximum-pool-size)
    hikari:
      maximum-pool-size: 10

  jpa:
    properties:
      hibernate:
        format_sql: false
        show_sql: false
        # Hibernate dialect is auto-detected except for H2/Postgres.
        # If using H2:     ca.uhn.fhir.jpa.model.dialect.HapiFhirH2Dialect
        # If using Postgres: ca.uhn.fhir.jpa.model.dialect.HapiFhirPostgresDialect
        dialect: ca.uhn.fhir.jpa.model.dialect.HapiFhirH2Dialect

        # --- Optional Hibernate DDL & tuning (commented out from source) ---
        hbm2ddl:
          auto: update
        jdbc:
          batch_size: 20
        cache:
          use_query_cache: false
          use_second_level_cache: false
          use_structured_entries: false
          use_minimal_puts: false

        # --- Hibernate Search (Lucene/Elasticsearch) ---
        search:
          enabled: false
          # Lucene backend (default example)
          # backend:
          #   type: lucene
          #   analysis:
          #     configurer: ca.uhn.fhir.jpa.search.HapiHSearchAnalysisConfigurers$HapiLuceneAnalysisConfigurer
          #   directory:
          #     type: local-filesystem
          #     root: target/lucenefiles
          #   lucene_version: lucene_current
          # Elasticsearch backend (alternative) — see also hapi.fhir.elasticsearch section in docs
          # backend:
          #   type: elasticsearch
          #   analysis:
          #     configurer: ca.uhn.fhir.jpa.search.HapiHSearchAnalysisConfigurers$HapiElasticAnalysisConfigurer

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# HAPI FHIR — grouped by domain
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
hapi:
  fhir:

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # A. Core Server & API
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    openapi_enabled: true                       # Swagger UI at /fhir/swagger-ui/index.html; API docs at /fhir/api-docs
    fhir_version: R4                            # DSTU2 | DSTU3 | R4 | R5
    # use_apache_address_strategy: false
    # use_apache_address_strategy_https: false
    # custom_content_path: ./custom               # folder name must be 'custom'
    # app_content_path: ./configs/app            # served under /web/app
    # server_address: http://hapi.fhir.org/baseR4
    # defer_indexing_for_codesystems_of_size: 101

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # B. Implementation Guides (IG) & Package Install
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    ig_runtime_upload_enabled: false
    # validate_resource_status_for_package_upload: false   # default true
    # install_transitive_ig_dependencies: true
    implementationguides:
      cql:
        name: hl7.fhir.uv.cql
        version: 2.0.0
        installMode: STORE_AND_INSTALL
        installResourceTypes: [ "CodeSystem", "ValueSet", "ConceptMap", "ActivityDefinition", "PlanDefinition", "Library", "Measure", "StructureDefinition" ]
      uscql:
        name: hl7.fhir.us.cql
        version: 1.0.0
        installMode: STORE_AND_INSTALL
        installResourceTypes: [ "CodeSystem", "ValueSet", "ConceptMap", "ActivityDefinition", "PlanDefinition", "Library", "Measure", "StructureDefinition" ]
    #   swiss:
    #     name: swiss.mednet.fhir
    #     version: 0.8.0
    #     reloadExisting: false
    #     installMode: STORE_AND_INSTALL
    #   ips_1_0_0:
    #     packageUrl: https://costateixeira.github.io/smart-ips-pilgrimage-fulltest/package.tgz
    #     name: smart.who.int.ips-pilgrimage-test
    #     version: 0.1.0
    #     installMode: STORE_AND_INSTALL
    # additionalResourceFolders:
    #   - example
    #   - example2
    # supported_resource_types:
    #   - Patient
    #   - Observation
    # allowed_bundle_types: COLLECTION,DOCUMENT,MESSAGE,TRANSACTION,TRANSACTIONRESPONSE,BATCH,BATCHRESPONSE,HISTORY,SEARCHSET

# Simple Bearer-Token Authentication

A deliberately minimal authentication layer for the HAPI FHIR JPA Server.

- Log in with username/password → receive an opaque token.
- Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every FHIR request.
- Missing / invalid / expired token → `HTTP 401`.

**No OAuth2, no JWT, no Keycloak, no external identity provider.**

---

## Why it works (the one important detail)

HAPI's FHIR endpoint is **not** a Spring MVC controller. In
[`Application.java`](src/main/java/ca/uhn/fhir/jpa/starter/Application.java) the `RestfulServer` is
registered as a raw Jakarta **servlet** mapped at `/fhir/*`. Controller-level security
(`@PreAuthorize`, MVC interceptors) never runs for it.

The only layer that sits in front of *every* servlet is the **servlet filter chain**, where Spring
Security installs `springSecurityFilterChain`. Our `TokenAuthFilter` lives there, so it intercepts
`/fhir/*` even though those URLs are served by non-Spring code.

```
HTTP request
     │
     ▼
┌──────────────────────────────┐
│ springSecurityFilterChain     │  ← TokenAuthFilter runs here
│   (servlet filter)            │
└──────────────────────────────┘
     │ authenticated?
     ├── /fhir/*  → RestfulServer servlet (HAPI)
     ├── /auth/*  → DispatcherServlet → AuthController
     └── /        → DispatcherServlet / static UI
```

---

## What was added

### Dependency (`pom.xml`)

```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
    <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-security</artifactId>
    <version>${spring_boot_version}</version>
</dependency>
```

### Package `ca.uhn.fhir.jpa.starter.security`

| File | Responsibility |
|------|----------------|
| `SecurityConfig.java` | Declares the `SecurityFilterChain`: stateless, CSRF off, public allow-list, everything else authenticated, registers `TokenAuthFilter` and the 401 entry point. |
| `TokenAuthFilter.java` | `OncePerRequestFilter` — reads `Authorization: Bearer`, validates via `TokenService`, populates the `SecurityContext`. Never rejects directly. |
| `TokenService.java` | Generates 256-bit `SecureRandom` opaque tokens, stores `token → (username, expiry)` in an in-memory `ConcurrentHashMap`; `issue` / `validate` / `revoke`. |
| `AuthController.java` | `POST /auth/login` and `POST /auth/logout`. Constant-time credential comparison. |
| `RestAuthenticationEntryPoint.java` | Writes a clean `401` JSON body instead of Spring's default HTML/redirect. |
| `AuthProperties.java` | `@ConfigurationProperties("hapi.auth")` — username, password, token TTL, enable switch. |
| `dto/LoginRequest.java` | Record `{ username, password }`. |
| `dto/LoginResponse.java` | Record `{ token, tokenType, expiresIn }`. |
| `dto/ErrorResponse.java` | Record `{ status, error, message, timestamp }`. |

### Config (`application.yaml`)

```yaml
hapi:
  auth:
    enabled: true
    username: ${HAPI_AUTH_USERNAME:admin}
    password: ${HAPI_AUTH_PASSWORD:admin123}
    token-validity-seconds: ${HAPI_AUTH_TOKEN_TTL:3600}   # 0 = never expires
```

Set `enabled: false` to open the server again without removing code. Override the password via the
`HAPI_AUTH_PASSWORD` environment variable in production — never ship the default.

---

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Access |
|--------|------|--------|
| `POST` | `/auth/login` | **public** — returns a token |
| `POST` | `/auth/logout` | revokes the presented token (returns `204`) |
| `GET`/`POST`/… | `/fhir/**` (Patient, Observation, Encounter, …) | 🔒 token required |
| `GET` | `/fhir/metadata` | 🔒 protected |
| `GET` | `/`, `/fhir/swagger-ui/**`, `/fhir/api-docs/**`, `/actuator/health` | **public** |

---

## Token approach

- **Generation** — 32 bytes (256 bits) from `java.security.SecureRandom`, Base64-URL encoded. The
  token is **opaque**: it carries no decodable data (unlike a JWT).
- **Storage** — server-side `ConcurrentHashMap` as `token → (username, expiresAt)`.
- **Validation** — look up the token; absent or past expiry → invalid (and evicted). Otherwise the
  request is authenticated as that user.
- **Revocation** — `logout` deletes the entry — instant, unlike a self-contained JWT.

---

## Running

### Option A — Docker (recommended, port 8085)

`docker-compose.yml` maps host **8085 → container 8080** and starts the app plus a Postgres
database. The `HAPI_AUTH_*` environment variables set the credentials (defaults shown below).

```bash
cd /home/user/IdeaProjects/hapi-fhir-jpaserver-starter

# 1 · build the image (compiles the auth code) and start app + Postgres in the background
docker compose up --build -d

# 2 · follow the logs until you see "Started Application"
docker compose logs -f hapi-fhir-jpaserver-start

# 3 · sanity checks
curl -i http://localhost:8085/actuator/health        # → 200 (public)
curl -i http://localhost:8085/fhir/Patient           # → 401 (auth working, no token)
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8085/auth/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"admin","password":"admin123"}'     # → { "token": "..." }

# stop when done
docker compose down            # keep the DB volume
# docker compose down -v       # also wipe Postgres data
```

Credentials live in `docker-compose.yml` under the app service's `environment:` block:

```yaml
HAPI_AUTH_ENABLED: "true"
HAPI_AUTH_USERNAME: "admin"
HAPI_AUTH_PASSWORD: "admin123"      # change me in production
HAPI_AUTH_TOKEN_TTL: "3600"         # seconds (0 = never expires)
```

### Option B — Local (Maven, port 8080)

```bash
mvn spring-boot:run            # or: java -jar target/ROOT.war
# server: http://localhost:8080/fhir      UI: http://localhost:8080/
```

> **Port note:** Docker → `8085`, local Maven → `8080`. The curl examples below use `8080`;
> for Docker, swap in `8085`. In the Postman collection set `serverUrl`/`baseUrl` to match.

---

## Testing — curl

```bash
# 1 · log in → get a token
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/auth/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"admin","password":"admin123"}'
# → {"token":"...","tokenType":"Bearer","expiresIn":3600}

# 2 · capture it
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/auth/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"admin","password":"admin123"}' | jq -r .token)

# 3 · authenticated FHIR read → 200 + Bundle
curl -i http://localhost:8080/fhir/Patient -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

# 4 · no token → 401
curl -i http://localhost:8080/fhir/Patient

# 5 · wrong token → 401
curl -i http://localhost:8080/fhir/Patient -H "Authorization: Bearer nope"

# 6 · bad credentials → 401
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:8080/auth/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"admin","password":"wrong"}'

# 7 · log out (revoke) → 204
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:8080/auth/logout -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

## Testing — Postman

Import **`HAPI FHIR R4 - Core APIs.postman_collection.json`** (already wired for auth):

1. Run **Auth → Login (get token)** — its post-response script auto-stores the token in `{{token}}`.
2. Run any FHIR request — the collection sends `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}` automatically.
3. Optional: **Login - bad credentials** → 401, **Get Patient - NO token** → 401.

Collection variables — set these to match how you're running the server:

| Variable | Docker | Local Maven |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `serverUrl` | `http://localhost:8085` | `http://localhost:8080` |
| `baseUrl` | `http://localhost:8085/fhir` | `http://localhost:8080/fhir` |

(The collection ships pointed at **8085** for Docker.)

---

## Trade-offs

**Pros**

- Tiny footprint — one starter dependency, no JWT/OAuth machinery.
- Instant revocation (delete the entry → token is dead).
- Opaque tokens leak no decodable data if intercepted.
- One choke point secures the HAPI servlet *and* Spring MVC.
- Easy to read, test, and reason about.

**Cons**

- In-memory store: tokens vanish on restart and are **not** shared across instances — scaling needs
  a shared store (Redis/DB) or sticky sessions.
- Coarse-grained: a single admin identity, no roles/scopes/per-resource rules.
- A bearer credential is only as safe as the transport — **HTTPS is mandatory** in production.
- No standard client tooling, unlike SMART/OAuth.

changes.content: - **Responsibility:** declares the single `SecurityFilterChain` bean that defines *who can reach
- **Why it exists:** Spring Boot auto-detects this bean and uses it instead of the default
"everything requires login" chain. It's the central place where the public allow-list, the
stateless policy, CSRF, and our custom filter are wired together.
- `sessionCreationPolicy(STATELESS)` — no `HttpSession`; auth is re-evaluated from the token on
- `csrf().disable()` — CSRF protection is for cookie/session browser flows; a stateless Bearer API
- `dispatcherTypeMatchers(FORWARD, ERROR).permitAll()` — so when a permitted page errors
internally and Spring forwards to `/error`, the security layer doesn't mask the real error with
- Honors `hapi.auth.enabled=false` → permits everything (kill-switch without code changes).
- **Responsibility:** on each request, read `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, validate it, and (if
valid) mark the request as authenticated.
- **Why it exists:** this is the actual enforcement point that runs inside the servlet filter chain
— the one layer that can guard HAPI's raw servlet (see §2).
- Extends `OncePerRequestFilter` (guaranteed to run exactly once per request).
- On a valid token it sets a `UsernamePasswordAuthenticationToken` (with a `ROLE_USER` authority)
- It **never rejects** the request itself — if the token is missing/invalid it simply leaves the
context empty and lets the authorization rules + entry point decide. This keeps all rejection
logic in one place and lets public paths through cleanly.
- **Responsibility:** generate, store, validate and revoke tokens.
- **Why it exists:** isolates *all* token state and crypto behind a small API, so the rest of the
code never touches raw randomness or the store — and so the store can later be swapped (e.g.
Redis) without touching the filter or controller.
- **Generation:** 32 bytes (256 bits) from `java.security.SecureRandom`, Base64-URL encoded → an
**opaque** token (carries no decodable data, unlike a JWT).
- **Validation:** lookup; absent or past `expiresAt` → invalid (and evicted on access).
- **Revocation:** `revoke()` removes the entry — instant, unlike a self-contained JWT.
- **Why it exists:** this is the only public door — it turns credentials into a token, and a token
into "revoked." Served by the `DispatcherServlet` at `/auth/*` (doesn't collide with `/fhir/*`).
- Bad credentials → `401`; success → `200` with `{ token, tokenType, expiresIn }`.
- `logout` reads the Bearer header and revokes that token → `204`.
- **Responsibility:** produce the response when an unauthenticated request hits a protected path.
- **Why it exists:** Spring Security's default would redirect to an HTML login page — wrong for an
API. This returns a clean JSON body and a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` header instead.
- **Key details:** writes `ErrorResponse` JSON with status `401` and a helpful message
- **Responsibility:** bind the `hapi.auth.*` settings into a typed object.
- **Why it exists:** keeps credentials and the token TTL out of source code and overridable by
environment variables (so prod can inject a real password without recompiling).
- **`LoginResponse`** — the success body `{ token, tokenType: "Bearer", expiresIn }`.
- **`ErrorResponse`** — the uniform error body `{ status, error, message, timestamp }` used for both
- **Why they exist:** explicit, self-documenting request/response shapes instead of raw maps; they
make the API contract obvious and stable.

└─ Collection → Authorization tab = Bearer Token, value {{token}}
└─ every FHIR request = "Inherit auth from parent"
└─ Postman auto-adds the header at send time:
1. Run **Auth → Login (get token)** once — token is stored in `{{token}}`.
2. Run any FHIR request — the Bearer header is added automatically.
3. Optional checks: **Login - bad credentials** → 401, **Get Patient - NO token** → 401.
